column1: # Sentinel rows (BENCH-AFF): timed by EVERY targeted bench (`cargo xtask bench --affected` / `bench-rows`), whatever
# changed. In one fat-LTO library any change can move an untouched function by code placement alone (MEM-K5c:
# memset_16 went 0.94 -> 1.13 on a change elsewhere), so the rows that carry most of real programs' time are always
# measured. Derivation (2026-10-10, from the call-frequency survey work/callfreq/weighted.tsv): every function of
# tier HOT or WARM with self_instr_share >= 0.002 (the share of all instructions real workloads spend in it), one
# row each at its most common argument class (the smallest budgeted size: 16 B for the copy/fill kernels, 64 B
# for the search kernels; arghist: 80% of calls <= 32 B), plus
# the 4 KiB row of the bulk memory kernels (a different code path: placement moves them separately, memset_4k).
# regexec/regcomp are WARM by call count but carry 12% of the instructions, more than any HOT function but strcoll.
# Columns: bench, row, function, self_instr_share. Re-derive when weighted.tsv is regenerated.
